# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Oxley's Butte for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## A Dull World A Three World Empire telescope catalogued LV-670 in 2096 and nobody looked twice. In 2115 a passing research vessel read lithium in the rock, and in 2120 a Weyland-Yutani probe confirmed it: huge deposits of a rare isotope, the kind of find that rewrites a sector's balance sheets.
## Landfall - The [bold]Trijent Corporation[/bold], a W-Y colonial development subsidiary, came down in 2129 with the research group that made the find. - The ship's captain, a devout follower of reformed Shinto, named the planet [bold]Raijin[/bold] after the god of thunder. The two dead moons became Fujin and Raitaro. - Months later the first prefabs went up at a river fork in the temperate north, under the butte that gave the town its name.
## The Dam A mine needs power. Trijent hired the [bold]Cebrini group[/bold] to wall off the river, and for twenty years the town lived on construction shifts, concrete dust and floodwater. The dam was finished in 2150. The Herald was born the same year, as a single sheet listing the names of the workers the river had taken while it was being built.
## The Lithium Years - Full colonization was declared in 2161. Most families now draw a Trijent or Cebrini wage; contractors run the haulage, the canteens and the bunkhouses. - The ore goes off-world to refiners who breed it into tritium, and cheap fusion fuel across human space owes more to this valley than anyone off it will admit. - The [bold]Neroid Sector Policing Authority[/bold] keeps the peace beside Company security. Residents learn early which of the two will turn up when a Company man is the one accused.
## 2175 That year the colony sent out urgent calls for specialists in xenoarchaeology and xenofauna. Off-world reporters picked them up. The Company called them false alarms, scandals in the TWE parliament buried the story, and no specialist ever stepped off a shuttle here that we know of. The Herald asked who sent those calls and why. We are still asking.
